## Appearance

Hugh is a tall, exceptionally good-looking youth with broad shoulders and an attractive overall appearance. He has wavy chestnut hair, an open face often featuring a mocking grin, and bright, mischievous eyes described as hazel or light brown. Although noted for his manly and handsome look, he recently appeared strikingly pale and thin upon returning home.

_Sources: [v1 CHAPTER XV. A Tempest in the School Teapot P16](../source/v01-c15.md#nw-v01-c15-p0016), [v1 CHAPTER XV. ## Personality

Hugh is a tall, manly youth with wavy chestnut hair and a mischievous, teasing nature toward every girl. Smart and studious, he holds unique perspectives alongside an appreciation for humor. He is motivated by a resolve to make the most of his life and contribute his utmost to it, as well as a need to cover his own college expenses.

_Sources: [v1 CHAPTER XV. A Tempest in the School Teapot P28](../source/v01-c15.md#nw-v01-c15-p0028), [v1 CHAPTER XV. ## History

During his school days in [Brierley](../codex/places.md#brierley), Hugh Carrow spent his time teasing his classmate [Nell](../character/nell-harcourt.md), who famously smashed a slate over his head in response. Years later, after saving [Nell](../character/nell-harcourt.md) from drowning in a pond, Hugh asked for her friendship, though she initially refused. When both applied to teach at the [Brierley](../codex/places.md#brierley) school, Hugh selflessly withdrew his application so [Nell](../character/nell-harcourt.md) could take the job, leading the two former rivals to reconcile and become friends. He went on to teach at [Pale Sands](../codex/places.md#pale-sands-hotel), returning home every Friday evening, while also spending time with [Nell](../character/nell-harcourt.md) discussing their ambitions and community efforts. Before heading to [Wexcombe College](../codex/places.md#wexcombe-college), where he became Freshman Class president and earned High Honors in Classics alongside the Cooper Prize, Hugh's affectionate gestures signaled a shift in their relationship. During his college years, Hugh comforted [Nell](../character/nell-harcourt.md) through academic and personal embarrassments and eventually proposed to her in a garden, though she rejected his romantic advances to preserve their friendship. Tensions grew between them when [Nell](../character/nell-harcourt.md) misconstrued rumors regarding Hugh and [Rowena Calder](../character/rowena-calder.md), prompting her to angrily break a gift from him and refuse to dance with him at the graduation ball. Upon returning home, Hugh fell critically ill with typhoid fever, surviving the ordeal just as [Nell](../character/nell-harcourt.md) realized her true feelings for him. After recovering, Hugh took [Nell](../character/nell-harcourt.md) on a walk to [Dinah](../character/dinah-wren.md) Wren's garden, where he confessed his enduring love, cleared up their past misunderstandings, and happily received her acceptance of his proposal.

_Sources: [v1 CHAPTER XV. A Tempest in the School Teapot P3](../source/v01-c15.md#nw-v01-c15-p0003), [v1 CHAPTER XV. ## Quotes

> "Nell, my actions were not especially noble. Being of slight assistance to you brought me pleasure. Will friendship exist between us from now on? Is my former misdeed truly pardoned by you?"
>
> — Hugh Carrow — [v1 CHAPTER XXXVIII. The Bend in the Road P52](../source/v01-c38.md#nw-v01-c38-p0052)

> "Elias Purdy returned from Regent’s today to spend Sunday, and he was supposed to carry out a book that Professor Garrick is loaning to me."
>
> — Hugh Carrow — [v2 VII The Pointing of Duty P19](../source/v02-c07.md#nw-v02-c07-p0019)

> "People say it’s a pleasant old town, complete with the most splendid natural park anywhere. The landscape there is supposed to be grand, from what I’ve been told."
>
> — Hugh Carrow — [v3 ch.Change P22](../source/v03-c01.md#nw-v03-c01-p0022)

> "Nell, you are merely fatigued. Come along, put everything out of your mind and go for a stroll with me—a trek back through the forest past the marsh. I ought to have something to display to you there."
>
> — Hugh Carrow — [v3 ch.Autumn P15](../source/v03-c02.md#nw-v03-c02-p0015)

> "No. It is only because of a thing I witnessed over there during spring that I know it ought to be. Hurry. We will act as if we are a pair of youngsters once more, and we will travel whichever way the wind blows."
>
> — Hugh Carrow — [v3 ch.Autumn P17](../source/v03-c02.md#nw-v03-c02-p0017)

### [Nell Harcourt](../character/nell-harcourt.md) · [the relationship](../relationships/hugh-carrow--nell-harcourt.md)

Hugh and [Nell](../character/nell-harcourt.md) have a complex history that began in school when he teased her about her hair, prompting her to smash a slate over his head and refuse to speak to or forgive him. Their initial hostility grew into an intense academic rivalry, but Hugh held romantic feelings for her, keeping a dropped rose of hers and eventually saving her from a sinking boat in a dory. Over time, their dynamic softened into a close friendship as fellow members of the B.V.I.S., complete with quiet walks together, and the two were even presumed by some to be married.

_Sources: [v1 CHAPTER XV. A Tempest in the School Teapot P3](../source/v01-c15.md#nw-v01-c15-p0003), [v1 CHAPTER XV. A Tempest in the School Teapot P16](../source/v01-c15.md#nw-v01-c15-p0016), [v1 CHAPTER XV. A Tempest in the School Teapot P34](../source/v01-c15.md#nw-v01-c15-p0034), +41 more_
